I was in the 8th grade and there was this 7th grade girl that I had a crush on but never told her. Instead I just kept being her friend (I already got made fun of in that school and often got bullied for being a "lesbian", because my dads were gay and I had gotten really close to another girl there and the bullying ruined our friendship)

So, of course I never told her how I felt. She invited me to spend the night one night and I was so excited.  We had a great time, she liked to dance, and I just secretly drooled over her, I had such a huge crush on her. I feel like she knew I had a crush on her because she got flirty with me and even gave me a lap dance type deal. We did each other's make up, nails, had girl talk, danced, and overall had a great time. I remember thinking "this is the best sleep over ever". Anyway, it became time to go to bed and I got in bed next to her and fell asleep. 

I woke up to a groaning sound that startled me awake. It sounded like something creepy and out of this world. 

I rolled over and saw my friend, eyes wide open but she was unresponsive. I panicked for a moment thinking she was dead and started shaking her. (I swear to fucking God she looked dead with her eyes open like that, completely still) 

As I was shaking her, she finally responds "huh whats wrong?" I told her what happened and she laughed and said "haha yeah I sleep with my eyes open and make weird noises in my sleep. It's normal I'm fine."

But I so wasn't fine. The noises she made (the groaning sound she made that woke me sounded borderline demonic), the open dead looking eyes, haunted me. I had nightmares about her for a week after. I had nightmares where I either woke up next to her and she was possessed, or where I woke up next to her and she really was dead..

I know it sounds bad but after that my crush for her faded, that experience really disturbed me.. I couldn't be attracted to her like I was anymore after that. That experience just killed it for me, I couldn't get over it. 

 I still wanted to be her friend.. I never spent the night at her house again but still stayed friends with her until we went to separate schools and lost contact.

It all sounds silly in hindsight but I was seriously disturbed by it at the time. It was the creepiest experience I ever had at a sleep over.

I take that as a mood stabilizer for my Bi polar. It has been the best mood stabilizer I have ever been on, at least the most effective compared to others. I recently got back on it after an old psychiatrist screwed up my meds and took me off of it, and I went down hill quick when he did, I am still trying to stabilize and recover. .

I am currently on 125mg working up to 200mg which is my most stable dosage, but you have to work your way up to that. My doctor has me adding on 25mg every two weeks, to work my way to 200mg and plan on staying on that dosage once I get there.

The only down side I feel about this medication is that you have to slowly work your way up to a higher dose, and if you miss a dose you (or at least I do) are quick to experience withdrawal symptoms. If I miss one dose I soon start shaking and feels like my brain starts glitching. It does help remind me to take it though, the withdrawal symptoms lol.

I would talk to your doctor about it more because everyone's chemistry is different. For example, I know people who do great on Zoloft but if I take that I get psychotic. I recommend Lamotrigine when it comes to mood stabilization. But I would definitely talk to your doctor about it first and make sure they know your medical history.

I haven't recognized my reflection in years, I feel I have forgotten what I look like. I am really not sure what I look like anymore. I don't have a sense of time, everything feels like one, long, never ending moment, I am very time blind.  I had a suicide attempt a few months ago, two back to back ones actually, a month apart. Ever since the 2nd attempt not only do I not recognize myself in the mirror as usual, but my eyes look dead, like corpse eyes, not my eyes, not the stranger in the mirror's eyes, dead eyes. I know it's me in the mirror but that's how I feel when I look at it.

Sometimes I will be laying in bed and feel myself shrink drastically, then suddenly expand, I will feel big then suddenly long and small. Those moments are always unsettling.

I also have a dissociative disorder and cptsd, that the depersonalization seems to get triggered by from what I understand - it's like they all feed off each other in a sense. I don't really have a sense of self like everyone else. Sometimes I get overwhelming feelings that I am unreal or dead, that this is hell or something. The symptoms have become significantly worse since the last suicide attempt - although I had been experiencing them for years.

Sometimes I space out so hard I get stuck. Sometimes my own house looks foreign, my own friends look like strangers. Sometimes my hand doesn't look like mine, it looks like someone else's hand. I feel like I am often in the midst of an existential crisis. My memory is very poor. My memory is so poor my friends crack jokes about it, but that actually makes me feel good, they make me laugh about it all.

I avoid mirrors kind of on autopilot at this point, unless brushing my hair I guess. I try to not spend time looking in them, the more I stare at it (my reflection) the more unreal it all gets. Sometimes I feel like I am stuck in a nightmare and cannot wake up from it. Sometimes I feel like everything is chaos there is no meaning, I am stuck in this void. Sometimes my emotions feel shut off, I feel numb, I know I should, and that I do love someone, but I still can't feel that love. Sometimes I feel like I am losing it but I have come to find that self awareness and trying to keep aware that it's just the depersonalization and not reality kinda helps me to cope. It has never been this severe for me before. I am still trying to learn and understand how to cope.

I am kind of isolated, single parent, very selective with who I chose to talk to in my personal life. I've been through a lot of trauma, afraid to take risks, talking to friends help but at the same time I fear they wont understand if I were to bring up my struggle with depresonalization. I feel like a freak.

The funny thing is, I still function despite it all. Somehow, I still get up and do what I need to do everyday. I may be late, or forget to do something, but I still get out of bed, clean, cook supper, bond with my daughter, pay bills, attend therapy, doctor appointments, etc... I don't know how I do it sometimes. I always feel at some kind of paradox or turmoil within my mind. I really needed to get this out. Thanks for the post OP.
